findings.title: Denial cache key joins name and folder with '_', so different resources can share one key
findings.body: userPermDenialCacheKey builds namespace.perm_<uid>_<action>_<name>_<parent> with '_' as the only separator. Names and folder UIDs can contain '_' (the fixtures use dashboards:uid:some_dashboard and folders:uid:some_folder_1, service_test.go:430 and :437). So dashboard 'a_b' in folder 'c' and dashboard 'a' in folder 'b_c' both produce the suffix _dashboards:read_a_b_c. A denial recorded for one is returned for the other by Check (service.go:116-121) for up to 30s, with no error or log. That is a silent false deny for a resource the user can read. Fix: encode the tuple unambiguously, for example as a JSON array or with length prefixes, or use a separator that cannot appear in a UID. The charset of UIDs is inferred from the test fixtures, not from a validator I read.
findings.originReason: userPermDenialCacheKey and the denial lookup are added by this diff.

verification.reason: The denial key joins name and folder with a bare '_', and legacy Grafana UIDs may contain '_' (validUIDCharPattern is a-zA-Z0-9-_). So name 'a_b'/folder 'c' and name 'a'/folder 'b_c' produce the same key, and a cached denial for one is returned by Check for the other.

findings.title: Denial cache key does not include identity type; anonymous:0 and render:0 share one entry
findings.body: permDenialKey is built from checkReq.Namespace, UserUID, Action, Name and ParentFolder, with no IdentityType. The tests use subjects anonymous:0 (service_test.go:803) and render:0 (service_test.go:853), and the subject parser takes the part after the colon as the UID (service_test.go:979 uses user:test-uid and the key uses test-uid). Both anonymous and renderer subjects therefore reduce to UserUID "0" and share denial entries. The renderer is always granted dashboards:read and folders:read (service.go:446-447). If an anonymous Check on the same dashboard is denied, a later renderer read of it hits the denial entry at service.go:117 and returns Allowed:false for up to 30s, with no error. Fix: add the identity type to the denial key. The ParseTypeID implementation is in the external authlib module and was not read, so the shared "0" UID rests on the test subjects.
findings.originReason: The denial cache and its key are new in this diff.

verification.reason: The denial key leaves out IdentityType. Both anonymous and render-service identities use ID "0" (user/identity.go:296-298 and authn/clients/render.go:44-49). A denial recorded for anonymous:0 on a dashboard is therefore returned for render:0, even though getRendererPermissions grants '*' for dashboards:read.

findings.title: 'Should deny on explicit cache deny entry' passes without the denial lookup
findings.body: The permCache entry is set to false (dashboards:uid:dash1: false). The DB fake has no permissions (setupService's fStore, service_test.go:1328 and :1386-1395). So the cached path, the DB fallback and the final result are all deny. Removing the permDenialCache check at service.go:117 would leave this test green. The comment 'Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked' says the cache should grant access, but the value is false. Fix: set the cached value to true, so that without the denial lookup Check returns allowed and the test fails.
findings.originReason: The test is added by this diff.

verification.reason: The cached map holds dashboards:uid:dash1=false, and checkPermission tests the value (scopeMap[scope]), so the cache path denies. The DB fallback then uses the empty fakeStore from setupService, gets an empty basic role, no teams and no permissions, and an empty folder tree, so it also denies without error. The test would pass with the denial lookup removed.

findings.title: No test covers the write of a denial entry
findings.body: The only denial test seeds permDenialCache by hand (service_test.go:979). Nothing checks that a Check denied by the database (service.go:153-155) is then answered from the denial cache on the next call. The write path, including its key, is untested.
findings.originReason: The denial write path is new in this diff.

verification.reason: The only test reference to permDenialCache is the manual Set at service_test.go:979. No test calls Check, gets a DB-backed denial and then checks that the denial entry is written (service.go:154) or reused.

findings.title: In-process client loses its 30s client-side cache; the PR body does not say why
findings.body: Before this change the in-process client was built by newRBACClient with cache.NewLocalCache(30s), as shown by the removed lines in the diff. It is now built with &NoopCache{} (rbac.go:101-105). The PR body only says 'improve authz caching'. Is dropping the client cache for in-process mode intended, for example to avoid a second, client-level layer of stale denials on top of the new server denial cache? Please state the reason in the PR body.
findings.originReason: The diff replaces newRBACClient with a NoopCache-backed client for the in-process path.

verification.reason: In the base, newRBACClient built the in-process client with a 30s LocalCache. The head builds it with &NoopCache{}, and only the remote client keeps the 30s cache. The question about intent is a fair one.

findings.title: cacheHit branches in TestService_getUserPermissions are dead
findings.body: The 'permissions from cache' case was removed (the diff), so no case sets cacheHit to true. The branches at service_test.go:367-369 and :388-390 can no longer run. Remove the field and branches, or keep a case that tests something real.
findings.originReason: The diff removed the only cacheHit:true case.

verification.reason: Both remaining test cases set cacheHit: false, so the branches at lines 367-369 and 388-389 never run. getUserPermissions also no longer reads permCache, so a cacheHit case would no longer make sense here.

findings.title: Case named 'should return error if store fails' asserts success
findings.body: The case at service_test.go:351 sets no error on the fake store and asserts require.NoError. Its name says the opposite. Rename it or make it set the failure. This was already in the file before the PR, but the PR edits this table.
findings.originReason: The misnamed case is unchanged from the base.

verification.reason: The case sets no err on the fake store, and the loop asserts require.NoError, so its name contradicts what it tests. The same case with the same name already exists in the base.

contracts.action: Check: denial cache short-circuit (returns deny before any cache or DB lookup)
contracts.before_after: Before, a denied Check re-ran getIdentityPermissions on every call, reading permCache for user and anonymous identities. After, a recorded denial returns Allowed:false before any cache or DB read, for shortCacheTTL (30s).
contracts.visible_effect: A user denied on a resource keeps being denied for up to 30s after a grant. The old permCache had the same 30s window for negative entries, so the delay is not new in length.
contracts.failure_mode: Key collisions (cache.go:31) and identity sharing (service.go:116) produce silent false denials. The response has no error.

contracts.action: Check: write denial entry after DB decision
contracts.before_after: New. A denial is recorded only when checkPermission returned without error and allowed is false.
contracts.failure_mode: A failed cache Set is logged by cacheWrap.Set (pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:88-91) and the DB result is still returned. No user-visible failure.

contracts.before_after: Before, the permCache read happened inside getUserPermissions after GetUserIdentifiers, and a negative cache hit was final. After, the read happens earlier. A cache miss or a cached not-allowed result falls through to the DB (service.go:139), so cached negatives are no longer final.
contracts.visible_effect: Allows still come from cache for up to 30s, as before. Denials now reach the DB unless the denial cache answers first.
contracts.failure_mode: An error from GetUserIdentifiers at line 123 is discarded. The DB path at line 139 repeats the lookup and returns the same error, so a failing lookup costs one extra store call. The renderer identity is counted as a cache miss at service.go:137, which changes the metric.

contracts.equivalent_path: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:186 (getIdentityPermissions, the only List path before this change)
contracts.before_after: Before, List always went through getIdentityPermissions and its permCache read. After, a cached map is used directly and a miss goes to getIdentityPermissions.
contracts.visible_effect: Same cache staleness as before. The list is built from the cached scope map by listPermission (service.go:194).
contracts.failure_mode: Same error handling as before on the DB path (service.go:187-191). A cached map with missing grants gives a shorter list for up to 30s, as before.

contracts.before_after: Same identity switch with no DB fallback. Renderer returns ErrNotFound (service.go:353-354), where getIdentityPermissions returns the wildcard map. Unsupported identities return an error in both.
contracts.visible_effect: None beyond the callers' behaviour above.
contracts.failure_mode: Errors are dropped by Check and List and retried on the DB path, so the same error is returned to the caller.

contracts.action: getUserPermissions and getAnonymousPermissions no longer read permCache
contracts.before_after: Before, getIdentityPermissions returned a permCache hit when present. After, it always reads through singleflight to the DB and writes permCache. Its only callers in service.go run after the cached path has missed.
contracts.visible_effect: None on the user path, because the cached path has already answered for hits.
contracts.failure_mode: Any future caller of getIdentityPermissions would hit the DB on every call. No such caller is in service.go.
contracts.open_question: Confirm that no other file in pkg/services/authz/rbac (models.go, tree.go, metrics.go) calls getIdentityPermissions or getUserPermissions. Those files were not read.

contracts.action: In-process authz client built without a client-side cache
contracts.equivalent_path: pkg/services/authz/rbac.go:160-167 (the LocalCache client used for the remote path); the removed newRBACClient in the diff used the same LocalCache for in-process mode
contracts.before_after: Before, in-process Check and List responses were cached in the authlib client for 30s. After, they are not cached on the client, and every call reaches the server, where the new server caches apply.
contracts.visible_effect: Permission changes take effect without the 30s client-side delay in in-process mode. Each call pays the gRPC in-process round trip and the server cache lookups.
contracts.failure_mode: No failure path is added in this code. The cost is latency and server load per call.

contracts.action: Remote and standalone authz client keeps its 30s client cache
contracts.equivalent_path: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:116-158 (the server-side denial cache, which is also used by the remote gRPC server through RegisterRBACAuthZService at rbac.go:203-212)
contracts.before_after: Unchanged on the client. The server now adds a 30s denial cache, so in remote mode a denial may be held in the client cache and the server denial cache at the same time.
contracts.visible_effect: Whether a grant is visible in remote mode takes up to the sum of the two windows. Depends on whether the authlib client caches denials, which was not read.
contracts.failure_mode: A grant may be delayed by up to about 60s in remote mode if the authlib client caches denials.
contracts.open_question: Does the authlib client cache Check denials as well as allows? The authlib source is outside the repository snapshot.

summary: Four files reviewed. The diff adds a server-side denial cache and cache-first allow reads in Check and List, and drops the in-process client cache. Two fix-level findings: the denial key is ambiguous because it joins name and folder with '_' (cache.go:31), and it does not include identity type, so anonymous:0 and render:0 share entries (service.go:116). One test (service_test.go:982) passes without the denial lookup because its cached value is false, not true. Other findings are consider-level: no test of the denial write path, an unexplained removal of the in-process cache, and cleanup in the test file. The ADR directory does not exist in the snapshot, so no ADR constraints were checked. Nothing was built or run.
